root_idea.summary: The root's central orientation is seeking or going toward a thing.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop commercial seeking and offering, sending or allowing livestock to pasture, imposing something upon someone, and related senses of release or dispatch. The mark-and-sign branch is treated as a divergent lexical development associated with سُومَة and سِيمَا.

senses.definition: To inflict or bring evil punishment or torment upon someone; to afflict.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ, the verb governs the person subjected to the punishment. The lexical evidence also records interpretations involving imposing, seeking, or making someone incur the punishment.

senses.definition: To pasture livestock; to send cattle out to graze, allowing them to pasture freely.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of cattle or camels that are taken out to pasture or left to graze by themselves. The Quranic occurrence has the second-person plural subject addressing those who pasture their livestock.

senses.definition: Marked or bearing a distinguishing sign.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic angel passage, this is an interpretation of مُسَوِّمِينَ in which the angels are identified by marks associated with their horses or equipment.
An alternative Quranic interpretation of مُسَوِّمِينَ in the angel passage; the participle may describe forces sent out for action rather than marked by signs.

senses.definition: Marked, branded, or identified by a distinguishing sign.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the marked horses and of the stones of baked clay. The mark may be understood as branding, contrasting color, a seal-like impression, an identifying inscription or name, or a sign distinguishing the stones as divinely sent for punishment.
An alternative interpretation in the Quranic passages about the horses and the stones; the horses may be sent to pasture or advanced with their riders, and the stones may be understood as sent forth.

senses.definition: Of goodly make or fine form.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation specifically associated with the Quranic expression الخَيْلُ المُسَوَّمَةُ, the marked or distinguished horses.

senses.definition: A mark, sign, token, or badge by which something is recognized or distinguished.
senses.usage_conditions: The sign may identify people or distinguish one condition from another; in the Quran it is associated with recognizable marks on faces or persons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going out in pursuit of a thing, or seeking to find, obtain, or take it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun of سَامَ; in commercial contexts, seeking to obtain a commodity or its sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of livestock, to pasture freely or rove while grazing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of cattle, camels, sheep, or goats that pasture by themselves where they please.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do as one pleases, or to leave someone free to do so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression خَلَّيْتُهُ وَسَوْمَهُ means that someone was left to act according to his own choice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass, go along, or move quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels and of wind or winds; the verbal noun can emphasize rapid passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go, hover, or circle around something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage reported of birds moving around an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To offer a commodity for sale, or seek its sale or purchase by stating a price.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of either seller or purchaser in commercial negotiation; the construction may involve offering, asking, or quoting the price of the commodity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose, require, or bring a difficult or unwanted affair upon someone; to constrain or abase him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical construction than the Quranic punishment usage, commonly associated with hardship, trouble, punishment, or humiliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep or cleave to something without quitting it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Form I construction meaning to remain attached to or persist in a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send horses or camels out to pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animals are sent to graze where they will.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave someone free to act, or entrust him with authority to decide over property or an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes leaving a person to do as he pleases and giving him discretionary control or judicial authority in a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge one's horses against a people and make havoc among them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A martial construction with the horses understood as the means of attack.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Making a horse sweat thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equestrian usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a distinguishing mark upon a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mark may be branding, a contrasting sign, or another feature by which the horse is recognized.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bargain, chaffer, or contend over the price of a commodity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal commercial construction in which one party offers a price and another seeks a lower or different price.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge a horse to run, or to mark it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are reported interpretations of a specialized Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast one's eye or eyes at someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with إِلَيْهِ بِبَصَرِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set a mark, token, or badge upon oneself by which one may be known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of distinguishing oneself in war or battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A land where camels pasture freely or roam to graze.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to land into which livestock go to pasture by themselves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Arabic status of this word is questioned in the lexical evidence; it also occurs in the hostile greeting السَّامُ عَلَيْكُمْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree whose wood is used for ships' masts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Identified in the evidence with the tree خَيْزُرَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow or cavity in the ground where water remains, stagnates, or collects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A natural depression capable of holding water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gold or silver in veins within stone, or an ingot of gold or silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote the veins collectively, a single vein, the metal, or an ingot according to the reported usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The price or value of a commodity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized verbal noun used in commercial expressions; it may describe an expensive or high price.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow dug in the ground near a well, apparently intended to hold water for cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is reported as سِيَمٌ, originally سِوَمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Natural magic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later usage reported as an application of the word, with a Persian origin noted in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two small hollows beneath a horse's eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An evil or harmful thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of a poetic occurrence; the evidence presents the interpretation as attributed rather than generally established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The species is not further identified in the supplied lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Roving freely; especially, livestock pasturing by themselves in open land rather than being fed with fodder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of cattle, camels, sheep, or goats sent out to graze where they will. A related plural form in a reported tradition is also interpreted as secure or free to roam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where cattle pasture freely or rove while grazing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-name or locative usage connected with livestock left to pasture themselves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of passage, or a quick passage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported alternative interpretation of the same word, attributed to poetic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A broad, thick wooden structural member, including a piece at the bottom of a door's side-posts; also a staff in the front of a camel howdah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Technical vocabulary for wooden components of doors and camel vehicles.

cautions: The Lane Quran citation rendered as [iii. 121] for مُسَوِّمِينَ is not converted into a modern verse location; the supplied QAC occurrence is independently located at 3:125.

The mark/sign forms سِيمَا and related spellings are linked lexically with the root in the supplied evidence, while the root-level source characterizes this branch as divergent from the central seeking orientation.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:swm:42806:g3:main reports سَامَةٌ as equivalent to سَاقَةٌ, but the supplied unit does not define سَاقَةٌ sufficiently to assign its precise meaning confidently.
